# An older Markdown render can replace HTML or attach stale widgets

## Context

Markdown renders highlighted code asynchronously, commits its HTML, then waits before adopting embedded Neo components, LivePreview, and Mermaid content.

## The Problem

Real Markdown instances on `50fcfc526c` reproduce two failures with controlled promises. Releasing the earlier syntax-highlight wait last replaces the current heading. Releasing the earlier mount delay last puts its widget into `activeComponents` even though the current HTML has only the new placeholder. If the owner is destroyed immediately before the delay resumes, the obsolete widget can still be created.

## The Architectural Reality

Design authority: `Markdown.value` is reactive and `afterSetValue` destroys the previous embedded instances before rendering the current input. `render({code})` also has a direct caller in the LivePreview unit suite. The existing latest-run guard in `LivePreview#doRunSource` supplies a local precedent for checking ownership after asynchronous work.

## The Fix

Give each Markdown render a current identity that clears when `value` changes. Verify that identity and owner liveness before publishing HTML and before adopting children after asynchronous boundaries. Keep direct rendering and current inputs' embedded content working.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Inverse highlighting completion keeps the latest HTML with real reactive value changes.
- [ ] An obsolete or destroyed render registers no child after the mount delay. It cannot strand a Neo instance off-tree.
- [ ] Markdown and LivePreview unit tests pass, and the existing headless Learning route and Mermaid tests pass.

## Out of Scope

Portal HTTP body settlement is tracked in #21899. `#21460` addressed obsolete additions in the Neo code executor.

Live check on 2026-11-22 covered the latest 20 open issues, open and closed stale Markdown searches, the prior LivePreview repair, recent A2A claims and own assignments. 68 open at the sweep. Memory Core and Knowledge Base returned no matching repair.
